messages:
Maya (ml-eng): FYI nightly-longctx eval flagged a nasty regression after the quant rollout. model=rw-xl-30b-q4_kv-int8, eval_id=nightly-longctx-v2/2026-07-18. lots of cases where the assistant drops the instruction mid-session around ~9k tokens. sample below.

Sam (evals): can you drop the eval id + exact model variant and a sample generation? quantized or fp16?

Maya (ml-eng): eval_id above, it's the int8/KV variant (canary pushed ~02:30 UTC). here's an excerpt from a failing generation: 
```
USER: Follow these steps and then produce the final summary. [~9.1k tokens of context including prior instructions]
ASSISTANT: ... (continues)
=== at token 9124 ===
INSTRUCTION: Now summarize the plan.
=== generation ===
... unrelated repeated fragment pulled from ~2k tokens earlier ...
<END>
```
The assistant never emits the requested final summary. looks as if instruction was lost/overwritten.

Kevin (infra): that screams kv-index wrap. grep logs for kv-seqnum boundaries. example from serving logs around the canary window:
```
2026-07-18T02:29:59Z [serving] kv-seqnum=65534 model=rw-xl-30b-q4_kv
2026-07-18T02:30:00Z [serving] kv-seqnum=65535 model=rw-xl-30b-q4_kv
2026-07-18T02:30:01Z [serving] kv-seqnum=0 model=rw-xl-30b-q4_kv  # wrap
```
That looks like a 16-bit counter overflow.

Ria (prod): I saw similar behaviour in staging after the quant rollout earlier. a runtime build changed a counter type in one module; might be related. can someone reproduce with long seq (>=11k)?

Sam (evals): starting a replay on dedicated-staging with seq_len=11500 --model=rw-xl-30b-q4_kv. confirmed a seqnum wrap at the same token boundary; saved full token+kv index trace to s3://redwood-traces/longctx/1898765432/trace.jsonl

Oncall Bot: Incident INC-2026-342 created by Maya: Long-context instruction loss after kv counter wrap. Priority=P2

Kevin (infra): quick fix candidate in runtime: bump kv counter from uint16 to uint32. small diff: 
```
- uint16_t kv_seqnum;
+ uint32_t kv_seqnum;
```
Raised PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/542

Sam (evals): canary-built PR #542 and replayed the same session; no wrap observed at 65535 and the instruction is preserved through 12k tokens. uploading traces to s3://redwood-traces/longctx/1898765432/after_fix/

Maya (ml-eng): next steps:
- Kevin: deploy canary with PR #542 to ~10% traffic, enable extra kv logging (kv_debug=true)
- Ria: add an assert in nightly-longctx harness to fail if kv-offset > seq_len
- Sam: re-run full nightly-longctx once canary shows stability
I'll monitor incident.

Kevin (infra): pushing canary now, enabling debug kv logs on canary nodes and sticky-canary to dedicated-staging for easier repro. also prepping rollback playbook for hosted quant rollout.

Ria (prod): adding a test in the eval harness to hit 2^16 boundaries and adding a short CR for the guard (RIA-CR-101).

Sam (evals): scheduled full re-run at 04:45 UTC after canary warm-up.

~2 hours later~

Sam (evals): PR #542 merged to main after canary held at 10%. nightly-longctx re-run passed all prompt sets. artifacts in s3://redwood-traces/longctx/1898765432/after_fix/.

Maya (ml-eng): closing INC-2026-342 after 24h monitoring. follow-ups: INF-542 (runtime counter audit / merge), RIA-CR-101 (eval guard), EVAL-1898 (long-seq CI smoke tests). assigning Kevin INF-543 to audit other counters found in batching code.

Kevin (infra): noted, filing INF-543 and adding a short checklist to the runtime PR template to double-check integer widths for sequence counters.

Maya (ml-eng): thanks everyone. rolling back hosted quant rollout until runtime fix is in stable channel to protect public users; dedicated customers unaffected for now. I'll add notes to the release postmortem. :thumbsup:
